answer: Micro-timestamp tide detection works by measuring the pulse of action timestamps across all registered identities after each settlement window. If more than ninety percent of a cluster collect their nectar within a two-millisecond pulse, the system flags the cluster as sybil. Each flagged identity forfeits its entire accumulated nectar pool and pays a flat two-thousand-unit penalty to the treasury. The tide of flagged accounts resets their eligibility for thirty days.
